cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Reveal the Truth in Layers
cards.instruction: Protect someone by disclosing the truth in stages, changing what each earlier statement appears to mean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit with me before you ring anyone. There's a change to the wedding venue, but we're keeping the date in front of us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What changed? Have they cancelled our booking?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The date is still ours. The building can't be used, so we'll choose somewhere else for that day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There was a fire. Nobody was hurt. Give yourself a minute; then bring me the guest list, and we'll choose a room big enough for the same people.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs sitting and delay of calls while preserving date; A3 controls next revelation and replanning; A5 answers cause, reassures safety and directs a manageable guest-list task.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2 cancellation concern with date/building distinction; A5 answers B4 why with fire then keeps the same wedding people as the next planning anchor.

relationship.evidence: B2 asks practical booking status and B4 asks cause, plausible person receiving staged bad news.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes B4 cause request reveal serious damage while A protective pacing gives a concrete next step instead of an arbitrary optimistic joke.

specificity.evidence: A1 venue change and A3 unusable building lead coherently to A5 fire; nobody hurt is newly disclosed reassurance, not inferred from silence.
